learning_outcomes.text: explain the fundamental tasks of an operating system
distinguish the basic architectures of common operating systems such as Linux, Unix, and Windows
use the system programming interface of POSIX-compliant systems (SUS)
name different forms of parallel processing
name the essential components of the process models of Linux and Windows operating systems
describe the difference between processes and threads and explain their possible uses as well as their advantages and disadvantages
explain several scheduling strategies and apply them in an abstract model
explain the functioning of virtual memory management and apply different strategies and algorithms for memory management in abstract models
explain the problems that occur with concurrent access to shared resources and know how relevant synchronization mechanisms can be used to prevent these problems
use simple mechanisms by which processes can communicate
name the services of a file system and explain them using a simple file system

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Tasks of an operating system
Processes and Threads: Parallel processing, process model, threads, scheduling (algorithms with time slices and priorities)
Memory management (*-Fit, Buddy algorithm, LRU, Clock algorithm)
Synchronization of processes and threads (Semaphores, Mutexes)
Communication of processes and threads (Pipes, Sockets)
